snippet.title: The press conference that stopped the world 😱💔 #Basketball #History #MagicJohnson
snippet.description: On November 7, 1991, Earvin "Magic" Johnson — five-time champion with the Los Angeles Lakers — announced he had tested positive for HIV and was retiring immediately. The detail most people still get wrong: he did not have AIDS. He had HIV — in 1991, most people thought that was a death sentence. His wife Cookie was pregnant; she and son EJ both tested HIV-negative. Magic later said he had contracted HIV through unprotected heterosexual sex, and became a face of HIV education worldwide. Fans still voted him into the 1992 All-Star Game, where he won MVP. That summer he won Olympic gold with the Dream Team, and in 1996 he returned to the Lakers for 32 more games. He walked in to end a career — and walked out having changed the world. So tell us: did that one announcement matter more than all five championships combined? #Basketball #History #MagicJohnson 📸 Magic 1980: El Gráfico, PD; Forum: Ken Lund, CC BY-SA 2.0; Dream Team: Hackman/USAF, PD; Magic 2014: Neon Tommy, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons).

snippet.title: A Look at Magic and Cookie Johnson's Photos Through the Years as the NBA Legend and#celebrity
snippet.description:
Earvin “Magic” Johnson was intrigued the minute he laid eyes on his future bride, Earleatha Kelly ,aka Cookie, at a party back in the ‘70s.

“I never asked her to dance,” he recalled to PEOPLE back in 2016. “I just watched her dance, and I said, ‘I’ve got to get to know that woman.” And that he did. He went on to get her number and the two communicated the entire time they were on Christmas break. By the time school opened the next semester, the two were a couple.

Though they went through some ups and downs, the pair wed on Sept. 14, 1991, in Magic’s hometown back in Michigan. They would go through some public hardships together, most prominently, Magic’s HIV diagnosis in 1991.

“It was difficult. We cried for a couple of days just holding each other,” the former Laker told PEOPLE. “[Cookie] thought it was a death sentence because that’s all we knew.”

Still, Cookie supported her husband, explaining why she wore a white suit to stand by Magic’s side the day he revealed the diagnosis to the world.

“I wore that white suit for a reason,” she told Gayle King. “I didn’t want to wear anything dark or black because to me, it’s what it symbolized. And the white suit, to me, symbolized brightness, like a future basically [and] positivity.”

Below, see photos of Magic, Cookie Johnson and their family as the NBA legend and famed businessman celebrates his 67th birthday today.

snippet.title: EJ Johnson's Mom Cookie Says Magic Johnson Has 'No Regrets' Quitting On Lakers
snippet.description:
Wednesday, April 10, 2019 - EJ Johnson rocks skin tight shorts and an animal print zip up top to dinner with mom Cookie at a Tom Ford event at Mr. Chow in Beverly Hills. On Tuesday night, EJ's father Magic Johnson suddenly resigned as Los Angeles Lakers team president via an impromptu press conference leaving the sports world in shock. "We're just happy for him. No Regrets." Cookie said of his departure. Adding, "We just know that he's happy and we're happy for him." #EJJohnson #MagicJohnson #LosAngelesLakers #CookieJohnson
